label: first copy step echoing a leading "1" in short sequences (too sparse)
explanation: Active on only 46 of 1M sequences, with weak activations (max 0.16). About 83% of the activation mass is at the first copy step (recall_idx 1, previous input <DEL>) where the fed-back input is the digit 1 and the original sequence started with 1. These are almost all short sequences (L 3-5), and the next output is usually s, f or x. The other activations are scattered over late original-phase steps (o, n, b inputs). It does not fire on any other copy steps or on the <DEL> step. The descriptive predicate catches most of the activations but has precision of about 0.3%: nearly all sequences that start with 1 never activate it, so the true trigger is much narrower than any simple rule. Magnitude is about the same everywhere and is not explained.
